result.summary: Disables peer announcement of periodic wallet transaction resubmissions when `-privatebroadcast` is enabled. Unconfirmed wallet transactions are still resubmitted to the local mempool, but `node::TxBroadcast::MEMPOOL_NO_BROADCAST` is used instead of broadcasting to all peers.
result.problem: Periodic wallet rebroadcasts announce unconfirmed transactions over standard P2P clearnet connections. For users relying on `-privatebroadcast` to conceal transaction origins, periodic resubmission (or rebroadcasts triggered by events like incoming payments) deanonymizes the node as the wallet owner.
evidence: PR description: 'for users opting into private broadcast, it seems a bridge too far for them to expect the current behavior. e.g. an incoming dust payment triggering your node to rebroadcast 24-36th later over clearnet'
Release notes: 'A transaction that was broadcast privately and later received back from the network was otherwise announced again from the node's own connections, which revealed its origin.'
result.card: Suppresses P2P peer announcements during periodic wallet transaction resubmission when `-privatebroadcast` is enabled, instead keeping transactions in the local mempool without re-announcing them. This prevents wallet rebroadcast cycles from leaking the originator's IP address over clearnet connections after an initial private broadcast. The issue affects users configuring `-privatebroadcast` to protect broadcast privacy.

risk.why: Unconfirmed transactions that were evicted network-wide will not be repropagated unless handled outside the standard wallet resend loop, potentially leaving them unconfirmed.
